title: Storage consumption tracking (foundational)
description: Storage is tracked per database and per collection: bytes used, growth per day, and quota headroom. Tracking reads filesystem and object-store counters rather than estimating. The numbers feed both capacity planning and per-database cost attribution. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Compute utilization tracking (foundational)
description: CPU and memory utilization are sampled per service and aggregated into utilization rates over time. Sustained high utilization triggers scaling review; sustained low utilization triggers rightsizing. Utilization data is what turns 'the system feels slow' into an actionable finding. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
samples = [0.62, 0.71, 0.68, 0.75]  # cpu utilization
avg = sum(samples) / len(samples)
print(f'avg CPU: {avg:.0%}', '-> review scaling' if avg > 0.7 else '-> healthy')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Resource and Cost Monitor practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Latency tracking with percentiles (foundational)
description: Request latencies are tracked as percentiles, p50, p95, and p99, because averages hide the slow tail users actually feel. Percentiles are computed over sliding windows so recent regressions surface quickly. A p99 regression with a flat p50 means a tail problem, which points at very different causes than a general slowdown. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
import statistics
lat = [12, 15, 11, 14, 13, 12, 400, 11, 13, 12]
qs = statistics.quantiles(lat, n=100)
print(f"p50: {qs[49]}ms | p99: {qs[98]}ms | avg hides the tail: {sum(lat)/len(lat):.0f}ms")
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Resource and Cost Monitor practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: API usage metering per key (foundational)
description: API calls are metered per key and per endpoint: counts, error rates, and data volume. Metering supports both rate limiting and usage-based cost attribution. Keys approaching their quota get warned before they get throttled. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Threshold alerting with cost rollup (foundational)
description: Thresholds on every tracked resource fire alerts with the current value, the threshold, and the trend. Alerts roll up into a daily cost and consumption summary per database. The rollup is what operators read; the alerts are what wake them. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
alerts = []
storage_gb, threshold = 23.1, 20.0
if storage_gb > threshold: alerts.append(f'storage {storage_gb}GB > {threshold}GB')
print('alerts:', alerts if alerts else 'none')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Resource and Cost Monitor practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
